description: We are a team focused on finding solutions beyond what is merely visible.
summary: GonaSense is a Web Platform that advices Gombe local Farmers and Neighboring Northeastern states on whatPlant rotation works best for them and also when to plant to avoid dry-spell and false rainfall onset.
details:
GonaSense Gona as in Farm in Hausa and Sense as in Satellite sensing helps farmers in Gombe State, Nigeria, decide which crops to plant after each other. It uses NASA satellite data to show how the weather over the past 24 years would have treated different crop choices, such as when the rains started, how long dry spells lasted, and how hot it got when crops were flowering.

Farmers pick their current crops and see them compared with other options. They can say what matters most to them, like saving water, earning more or improving the soil, and the options reorder right away. Each option is explained in plain words, with clear notes on what the data can’t tell us.


Many farmers in Gombe have limited internet and use simple phones, so we plan to bring GonaSense to them by text message (SMS). Text messages work on any phone and don’t need internet. Farmers could receive short, clear alerts, such as when the rains look ready to plant, when a long dry spell is likely, or when a hot spell could affect crops that are flowering. Messages would be sent in simple English and, later, in Hausa.

Extension officers could also share the messages with whole farming groups, so people without phones are still reached. As with everything in GonaSense, the messages will be advice to support farmers’ own judgment, never an order.

GonaSense is a helper, not a replacement for experience. The farmer’s own knowledge and local extension officers always come first.
